title: Error notices — every "couldn't load" box becomes the guide's red-tinted notice box

steps.path: Chat → type / → the skills list fails to load
steps.headline: A whole list that fails to load is now the red-tinted notice box, with Retry inside it at the right.
steps.changed: Today an error is a grey box with a small red dot. Proposed: the same red-tinted box with a red border that every other warning and error in the app already uses (your guide's rule). The dot is gone; the words stay normal grey.
steps.notice: 61 places in the app change at once — every error that can be retried or reported. This slide is a whole list failing (the big size).
steps.risk: The words are a little smaller (the notice box's size), and a one-line message sits level with the top of the Retry button rather than its middle.

steps.path: Resume session → the conversation list fails to load
steps.headline: An error inside a popup or a menu uses the notice box's slim one-line form.
steps.changed: The "inline" errors (inside a list, a menu or a card) become the slim red notice box — the same one approved for the provider notices — instead of a grey strip with a dot.
steps.notice: Long messages wrap to two lines inside the box; Retry stays at the right.

steps.path: Status bar → tags → your tags fail to load
steps.headline: Session details' "couldn't load your tags" line becomes the slim red notice box.
steps.changed: Grey strip with a red dot → slim red-tinted box with a red border, Retry inside at the right.
steps.notice: Same look on the close prompt and Organize, which share this card.

steps.path: Settings → Assistant settings → Specialists → the tiers fail to load
steps.headline: An error inside a setting's card is the slim red notice box, inside that card.
steps.changed: The grey box with a dot inside the "Specialist intelligence tiers" card becomes the slim red notice box in the same spot.
steps.notice: The card around it is a little shorter, because the slim box has less padding.

steps.path: Settings → Assistant settings → Permissions → your approvals can't be read
steps.headline: A "we don't know why" error keeps its title, words and Report bug / Diagnose, now in the red notice box.
steps.changed: The general kind of error (cause unknown) moves into the red-tinted box: title in normal colour, the explanation under it, and Report bug then Diagnose with the assistant on their own line at the bottom right, as before.
steps.notice: The title is a little smaller than today, matching every other notice's title. Whether it should have a title at all is the second question below.

steps.path: Settings → Assistant settings → General → the step guard fails to load
steps.headline: Step guard's hand-made error line with a bare text Retry becomes the shared notice box with a filled Retry.
steps.changed: This one was drawn by hand: a small red line with "Retry" as plain text inside it. It now uses the shared error box, so Retry is a real filled button at the right.
steps.notice: Also moved, with no practice screen to photograph: GitHub's connect error, the voice download failure, and the game connection error (its big red ! is gone).
steps.risk: GitHub's button changes from "Try again" to "Retry" until the first question below is answered.

steps.path: Marketplace → Your library → your plugins fail to load
steps.headline: Full screens (Library, Marketplace) get the same red notice box across the top of the list.
steps.changed: Grey band with a dot → red-tinted band with a red border, Retry at the right.
steps.notice: The Themes tab of the library changes the same way.

steps.path: Projects → a project → Files → a folder the computer won't open
steps.headline: A project folder that can't be opened shows the red notice box where its files would be.
steps.changed: Grey card with a dot → red-tinted card, same words, Retry inside at the right.
steps.notice: Same in a project's file search, a chat's files panel and the Office versions list.

steps.surface: Every error with a retry button
steps.path: Anywhere something fails and can be tried again
steps.headline: Should the retry button say "Retry" or "Try again" everywhere?
steps.today: The 61 shared error boxes say "Retry". The screens you redesigned recently (Games while offline, a failed ticket, Contribute, the close prompt, model providers) say "Try again", and your guide is written with "Try again".
steps.problem: Two words for the same button. Moving GitHub's connect error onto the shared box changed its "Try again" to "Retry", so the split now shows on one more screen.
steps.proposal: Pick one word and every error box uses it; the screens that hand-wrote the other word are changed to match.

options.label: Try again
pros: Matches the guide and every screen you approved this month
Plainer for people who are not technical
cons: About 61 places change wording, and the game error's hint ("you can also hit Retry") needs rewording

options.label: Retry
cons: About ten recently approved screens change from "Try again" to "Retry"

steps.path: e.g. Settings → Permissions when your approvals can't be read
steps.headline: Should "we don't know why" errors keep a bold title line, or say it in one sentence?
steps.today: These errors have a title ("Unable to show what you've approved.") and a sentence under it, then Report bug and Diagnose. Slide EN-5 shows it in the new box with the title kept.
steps.problem: Your guide says most notices need no title — one plain sentence says it — and the failed-ticket decision chose no title. The old error design always had one.
steps.proposal: Either keep the title as shown, or merge title and sentence into one plain paragraph with no bold line. About 9 places are this kind.

options.label: Keep the title
pros: The headline is easy to spot when the explanation is long
cons: A bold line that most other notices don't have

options.label: One plain paragraph
pros: Matches the guide's "one plain sentence" and the ticket's failed send
cons: Each of the 9 or so messages needs rewording so it still reads well without its headline
